rules.text: enqueue is idempotent by notification id for the lifetime of the outbox. A duplicate returns false, does not change pending state, and emits dedupe.
flush calls transport.persist for every pending item in insertion order before the first transport.publish; then publish runs in the same insertion order.
On any persist or publish failure, every item whose persist completed successfully is passed to transport.compensate in exact reverse persist order.
The original persist/publish Error object is rethrown unchanged. compensate failures never replace it; their message strings are appended in occurrence order to error.rollbackErrors.
Successful flush clears pending. Failed flush preserves the full pending list and insertion order for retry. The supplied transport is responsible for idempotency by notification id across retries.
Trace is append-only and copied on read. It records enqueue/dedupe and each persist/publish/compensate/compensate-error attempt in exact execution order.

callableSurface.ownership: The notification outbox owns dedupe history, pending order and trace. The caller owns transport side effects; transport methods are async and idempotent by item.id.

transitions: all stages and sends succeed -> committed/empty
stage/send failure -> reverse compensation then failed/pending

eventOrdering: all persist events precede the first publish in a flush
compensate events occur in reverse successful-persist order
compensate-error immediately follows its failed compensate attempt
failure preserves pending order before the original error is rethrown
abortErrorPrecedence: There is no abort surface. The original persist/publish failure has precedence over compensation failures and is rethrown unchanged.

identityMutation.inputs: enqueue payload objects and transport are never mutated
identityMutation.ids: dedupe is by exact id string and persists after success
identityMutation.trace: trace returns a new array with new event objects
